pillar_reactions.evidence: Tied it to his own diagnosis unprompted and argued the case for the rep — 'I bet that like for this, the kettlebells are way better than any gym... you really train these rotational moves with weights so it's basically like what you do in your life you are picking up heavy stuff... so if you will have strong core then most likely you will not get injured down the road.' He had already bought a 12kg kettlebell because of Trevor's videos.

Accepted the what/when/how-much framing and then asked a mechanics question that showed he had studied the content — 'I guess that Trevor is fasting as well during the morning, isn't he?' — and volunteered his own current rule, not eating after 6pm for sleep quality. Engaged rather than merely agreeing, but no resistance.

Volunteered a positive reaction and explained why it mattered to him specifically — 'this is really interesting. And it's amazing that you guys do something like that... that you are trying to really, for the client to not lose the workout and just go around it so he can still have the benefit of working out. Because this is the tricky part where most of the people fall off.' This was the pillar aimed directly at his named gap and it drew the strongest reaction of the three.

anchors.raw: I've spent this when I was in Africa for 10 days last year, right? And this, you are talking about six months fully dialed-in program. And it's not a vacation, right? It's not a leisure. It's your life.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor, and the prospect supplied it himself without prompting. A recent discretionary $6,000 spend on a 10-day holiday made six months of coaching look proportionate. The rep did not have to build value against it — he stayed quiet and let it work.

anchors.raw: the surgery that you would get on your back would be probably double the price
anchors.note: Self-generated cost-of-inaction anchor against future medical spend. Note the prospect immediately undercut his own point, which the rep did not pick up on.

anchors.raw: I don't, you know, in Czech Republic, I think the surgery would be, you know, for, I don't want to say for free, but I think that the insurance would cover all of it.
anchors.note: Materially weakens the avoid-future-medical-cost frame in any single-payer market. The prospect talked himself out of it — 'But it's not about that' — but for European prospects generally the cost-of-inaction argument cannot lean on surgery pricing.

anchors.raw: I also bought my first kettlebell, I think like three months ago, 12 kilos.
anchors.note: A free substitute already in use and already producing partial results — he does the morning routines daily and imitates the kettlebell sessions. The founder's organic content is simultaneously the lead source and the cheapest competitor; the counter here was uncertainty about technique, which is genuinely the right wedge.

anchors.raw: the only thing is that my credit cards are probably going to hold me onto this, because my limits are not this high to pay in one amount.
anchors.note: Not a value objection but a transaction ceiling — willingness exceeded card capacity. This is what forced the two-pay, and it is a recurring practical constraint for non-US prospects that the script has no step for.

unmet_demand.want: Something that lasts beyond the engagement — he explicitly did not want a six-month intervention but a permanent change in how he trains.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a defined six-month container and nothing was said about what happens after it. He raised this himself — 'I don't want to do this like for now for six months but I hope that it's gonna last me for forever and then I just gonna stay with it because I want to be mobile when I'm gonna be 70 or 80' — and the rep did not respond to it, then later used the six-month boundary as a closing argument instead ('the six months, that's not really a lot of time').

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that his back condition is safe to train around, and a plan built with reference to his MRI findings.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He disclosed a displaced vertebra and a doctor's assessment, and asked implicitly where kettlebells could take him — 'I don't know where that could take me. And that is also a reason why I'm here as well.' No clearance was sought, no clinician contact was proposed, and the MRI was never mentioned again after 00:17:44. Whether the programme can safely serve a diagnosed spondylolisthesis is genuinely unknown from this call and needs a human and clinical answer, not a sales one.

unmet_demand.want: To involve his wife in a $6,000 household decision before committing.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not a product gap at all — the process simply did not accommodate it. He stated the need plainly and it was neither refused nor honoured, just passed over, and he paid on the same call. Flagged here because it is demand the sales process left unserved rather than demand the product cannot meet.
